Hydrological implications of satellite-based water budget in the source area of China’s South-to-North water transfer middle route project
Warming, snow loss and drought intensification in Mediterranean water towers: The Ebro River basin and the Spanish Pyrenees
abstract: Mountains provide essential water resources for dry lowlands, and in the semi-arid Mediterranean, seasonal snow and high-elevation rainfall sustain downstream urban and agricultural areas. As these regions are highly vulnerable to climate change, reliable regionalized CMIP6 projections are critical. This study focuses on the Ebro River Basin and the Spanish Pyrenees, producing regionalized temperature and precipitation datasets for four Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP1-2.6, SSP2-4.5, SSP3-7.0, and SSP5-8.5), modelling future snow cover, and calculating the Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index (SPEI) to assess drought conditions. This is the first basin-scale CMIP6-based analysis for the Ebro River Basin that combines temperature, precipitation, Snow Water Equivalent (SWE) balance, and drought severity metrics (SPEI). Multi-model mean temperatures are projected to rise across the basin, with maximum temperature increases ranging from 0.58 °C to 4.53 °C and minimum temperature from 0.32 °C to 3.31 °C depending on the scenario. Multi-model mean precipitation shows no significant decline under SSP1–2.6, but local decreases of up to − 410 mm, accumulated over the study period, emerge under SSP5–8.5 in the northern Pyrenean headwaters. Our snow modelling reveals widespread cover loss under all scenarios, while SPEI results show droughts intensifying in severity and in frequency under all scenarios except SSP1-2.6, where a slight decrease is observed. These projections provide a basis for anticipating combined risks and supporting adaptation strategies. The integrated use of regionalized climate projections, snow modelling, and drought assessment provides a spatially explicit framework for identifying these interacting hydroclimatic changes and their potential implications for water-resource management and climate adaptation in the Ebro River Basin and the Spanish Pyrenees.

title: A structure-constrained inverse distance weighting framework for stochastic simulation of multi-lithofacies sedimentary aquifer architecture
abstract: Characterizing multi-lithofacies aquifer architecture from sparse borehole data is essential for groundwater flow and solute transport modeling, yet remains challenging because categorical lithofacies fields must honor hard conditioning data while representing realistic proportions, anisotropic continuity, and connectivity. Conventional inverse distance weighting (IDW) is transparent and computationally efficient but primarily produces a single deterministic estimate and does not provide stochastic categorical realizations or categorical uncertainty. This study develops a bias-corrected inverse distance weighting (BIDW) framework for conditional stochastic simulation of heterogeneous aquifer architecture. At each unsimulated cell, anisotropic IDW support is used to construct a local categorical sampling distribution, from which lithofacies are sampled sequentially to generate borehole-conditioned stochastic skeletons. Subsequent structural organization and refinement uses lithofacies proportions and directional mean lengths as soft constraints, with tunable structural-reinforcement settings. Based on a three-lithofacies 3D synthetic aquifer benchmark, the staged workflow progressively improved grid scale agreement, with mean overall accuracy increasing from 0.668 to 0.716. The high-proportion background lithofacies was reproduced with a largest connected component fraction of 0.999 and directional mean lengths close to those of the reference model. For the low-proportion lithofacies, the number of connected components decreased from 423.4 to 18.4, close to the reference value of 16, while the largest connected component fraction increased from 0.401 to 0.747. These results demonstrate that BIDW effectively extends IDW from deterministic interpolation to stochastic structural simulation, providing a transparent, data-efficient, and geologically constrained alternative for borehole-based aquifer architecture modeling.

title: N-tuple collocation for reference-free uncertainty estimation from multi-source hydrological data: beyond triple collocation and three-cornered hat
